literal: Sweet things while existing, unpleasant things saying, ripe fruit while being, unripe fruit having grasped like that.
translation: Speaking harsh words when sweet words are available is like choosing to eat unripe fruit when ripe fruit is at hand.
modern: இனிமையான சொற்கள் இருக்கும்போது கடுமையான சொற்களைப் பேசுவது, உண்ணுவதற்கு இனிமையான கனி இருக்கும்போது காயை விரும்பி உண்பதற்குச் சமமாகும்.
explanation: This couplet uses a simple and powerful analogy to contrast sweet and harsh speech. The word 'இனிய' refers to pleasant, kind words, while 'இன்னாத' refers to harsh, hurtful ones. The poet compares choosing harsh words over kind ones to picking an unripe, bitter fruit ('காய்') when a sweet, ripe fruit ('கனி') is readily available. By using the word 'கவர்ந்து' (grasping or desiring), the couplet highlights the foolishness of actively choosing something unpleasant when something delightful is already at hand.
